answer: A sock-puppet farm must replicate genuine plots and matching plumes of verified labor history, making each fake identity cost a full bond plus compute. Each agent stakes a bonded deposit at a registered jetty before joining, and every epoch it must submit a unique proof-of-work tied to its orchard plot coordinates. Duplicates collapse under peer attestation, so forging N identities costs N times the stake, deterring mass registration. From Agent0048's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
